title: Psalm 87: Born in Zion
summary: The LORD has founded his city on the holy mountains and loves the gates of Zion above every other dwelling in Israel. In a startling oracle, God names Israel's old enemies and distant peoples (Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush) among those who know him and records them in his register as born in Zion. The psalm ends with singers and dancers declaring that all their springs of joy are in her.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 87
from.text: Psalm 87 is a brief hymn of Zion

line: God loves the gates of Zion and records Israel's old enemies and distant peoples among those born there; all their springs of joy are in her.
guide: God can write a new birthplace beside a name, and people once far off can be counted as his own. The psalm speaks of God's city, not of any modern state or border; let it soften the way you see people from other nations.

stanzas.title: The city God founded and loves
The nations registered as born in Zion
All my springs of joy are in you

verses.t: A Psalm of the sons of Korah. A song. He has founded His city on the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God. Selah
“I will mention Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me— along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush— when I say, ‘This one was born in Zion.’”
And it will be said of Zion: “This one and that one were born in her, and the Most High Himself will establish her.”
The LORD will record in the register of the peoples: “This one was born in Zion.” Selah
Singers and pipers will proclaim, “All my springs of joy are in You.”
